variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network that assigns probabilities to the next token in a sequence. It turns a prompt into tokens, uses the tokens that fit in its context window, scores possible continuations, and decodes one token at a time into a response.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Follow one prediction from prompt to response”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Encode the request
pairs.detail: Tokenization maps text to vocabulary IDs.
pairs.explanation: Tokenization maps text to vocabulary IDs. The model can only operate on the resulting IDs and the text preserved in its context window.

pairs.label: Build a context-conditioned score
pairs.detail: Transformer layers combine the retained tokens into a score, called a logit, for every possible next token.
pairs.explanation: Transformer layers combine the retained tokens into a score, called a logit, for every possible next token.

pairs.label: Form a candidate distribution
pairs.explanation: Softmax converts scores into probabilities. Temperature changes how concentrated that distribution is; it does not add evidence.

pairs.label: Decode and repeat
pairs.detail: Greedy decoding takes the highest-probability token.
pairs.explanation: Greedy decoding takes the highest-probability token. Sampling draws from an allowed set, then repeats the cycle with the chosen token appended.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. This lesson assumes model evaluation.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Encode the request: Tokenization maps text to vocabulary IDs. Build a context-conditioned score: Transformer layers combine the retained tokens into a score, called a logit, for every possible next token. Form a candidate distribution: Softmax converts scores into probabilities. Decode and repeat: Greedy decoding takes the highest-probability token.

pairs.label: Retrieve
pairs.detail: Fetch current, permissioned sources and rank them for the request.
pairs.explanation: Fetch current, permissioned sources and rank them for the request. Retrieval quality sets an upper bound on what the model can ground in.

pairs.label: Fit
pairs.detail: Reserve tokens for instructions, source excerpts, tool output, and the answer.
pairs.explanation: Reserve tokens for instructions, source excerpts, tool output, and the answer. Summaries and truncation can discard the decisive detail.

pairs.label: Verify
pairs.detail: Check citations, execute authoritative tools, or route uncertain cases to review.
pairs.explanation: Check citations, execute authoritative tools, or route uncertain cases to review. The right verifier depends on the consequence of being wrong.

pairs.label: Pre-train
pairs.detail: Predict the next token across broad data.
pairs.explanation: Predict the next token across broad data. This teaches patterns in language and code, but it does not guarantee that a particular answer is current or correct.

pairs.label: Post-train
pairs.detail: Use demonstrations, preference data, or task examples to improve instruction following, format control, and desired response behavior.
pairs.explanation: Use demonstrations, preference data, or task examples to improve instruction following, format control, and desired response behavior.

pairs.label: Evaluate
pairs.detail: Measure task quality, calibration, safety, factuality, and failure slices with held-out data and human review where needed.
pairs.explanation: Measure task quality, calibration, safety, factuality, and failure slices with held-out data and human review where needed.

pairs.label: Operate
pairs.detail: Version prompts and models, observe retrieval and tool traces, and make rollback possible when quality, cost, or safety regresses.
pairs.explanation: Version prompts and models, observe retrieval and tool traces, and make rollback possible when quality, cost, or safety regresses.

variants.prompt: What does a high probability for the next token establish?
options: The token is true in the external world
The token is a likely continuation given the model, retained context, and decoding setup
The token appears in the training corpus
A verifier approved the claim
variants.explanation: A next-token probability ranks continuations under a conditional distribution. It is not independent evidence that a claim is true.

variants.prompt: Why can top-p sampling change an answer even when the prompt and model are unchanged?
options: It permanently updates model weights
It removes low-ranked probability mass and samples from the remaining normalized candidates
It retrieves new documents
It gives every vocabulary token the same probability
variants.explanation: Top-p forms a candidate set from cumulative probability mass and renormalizes it. Sampling can then choose different allowed continuations.

variants.prompt: What does raising temperature do to a fixed set of logits?
options: It adds new evidence to the prompt
It usually flattens the probability distribution and raises sampling diversity
It guarantees a factual answer
It increases the context window
variants.explanation: Temperature rescales logits before softmax. A higher temperature generally makes the distribution less concentrated; it does not verify content.
